newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up on electronics, China-concept.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up on electronics, China-concept.

text.p: Active buying in Taiwan's star electronics sector and China-concept stocks pushed share prices to close sharply higher on Friday, brokers said.
The index surged as high as 8,353.65 before settling for a closing gain of 111.64 points or 1.36 percent at 8,342.94.
Turnover was an active T$138.9 billion.
Electronics surged 4.23 percent, partly reflecting U.S. high-tech shares' overnight rebound, with chipmaker United Microelectronics up T$3.5 to T$85.5, brokers said.
Chipmaker Mosel surged T$3.5 to T$72.5 and computer gaint Acer rose T$2.5 to T$84.
China-concept shares -- Taiwan firms with active or planned investments in the communist Chinese mainland -- were strong, and those in electronics even more so.
China-linked power supply maker Liton Electronic surged the daily seven percent limit to T$101.5.
"A firming trend no doubt has set in, and it will be led by electronics and China-concept shares," said United Securities vice-president Lin Long-hsien.
Brokers noted many institutional investors have turned their recent short positions to active buying, something that has boosted overall sentiment.
The index opened higher after three major banks followed the Bank of Taiwan and cut various interest rates from Friday, a move that brokers said would drive up stock market liquidity.

Taiwan Cooperative Bank and Farmers Bank of China said they would cut their prime rates, while First Commerical Bank, one of the island's "big three" state-run banks, said it would cut various time deposits rates.
The rate cuts became effective from Friday.
Leading venture capital and investment firm, China Development, surged T$5 to T$122, reflecting a recent surge in electronics, where the firm is heavily invested.
